text.title: C# Clean Architecture + CQRS Failure Modes
text.summary: 14 antipatterns observed in real Clean Architecture deployments, including the AI-specific ones. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Domain entities become property bags; every business rule sits in `UserService` handlers. Code review shows zero non-getter methods on `User`.
antipattern.root-cause: Agent adds new behaviour to Application handler instead of the Domain entity.
antipattern.fix: Move the rule onto an entity method (`user.Activate()`). Prompt agents to open `Domain/Entities/<Aggregate>.cs` first when changing behaviour.

antipattern.symptom: Application project compiles with `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;`. NetArchTest run is missing or skipped in CI.
antipattern.root-cause: Author imported EF into Application "for convenience" and reviewer let it land.
antipattern.fix: Enable a NetArchTest fitness assertion: `Types.InAssembly(Application).Should().NotHaveDependencyOn("Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore")`. Fail the build.

antipattern.symptom: Cross-aggregate handler triggered inside `SaveChangesAsync`; downstream failure rolls back the originating write unexpectedly.
antipattern.root-cause: Domain events dispatched inline instead of via outbox.
antipattern.fix: Persist domain events to an outbox table inside the same transaction; dispatch asynchronously via MassTransit Outbox or a hosted relay.

antipattern.symptom: `GET /health` wrapped in `GetHealthQuery`/`GetHealthQueryHandler`; profile shows handler resolution dominating request latency.
antipattern.root-cause: Every endpoint dispatched through MediatR by default.
antipattern.fix: Reserve MediatR for use-cases that benefit from the pipeline (validation, auth, transaction). Trivial reads stay as plain controller actions.

antipattern.symptom: Handler does `user.Posts.Add(post)`; invariants bypassed; domain events not raised.
antipattern.root-cause: Collection exposed as mutable `ICollection<T>` and mutated directly.
antipattern.fix: Expose collections as `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`; mutate via aggregate methods (`user.AddPost(post)`). Raise the domain event inside the aggregate.

antipattern.symptom: Multi-tenant query returns rows from other tenants in production; audit log shows `IgnoreQueryFilters()` in a non-admin repository.

root-cause.source: EF Core docs — global query filters

antipattern.root-cause: Agent reached for `IgnoreQueryFilters()` to "see all rows" and shipped it.
antipattern.fix: Forbid `IgnoreQueryFilters()` outside `Infrastructure/Admin/` via a Roslyn analyzer rule; require code review approval for any new use.

antipattern.symptom: `INotificationHandler<T>` declared `async void`; one unhandled exception inside the handler tears down the host.
antipattern.fix: Return `Task`. The Notification dispatch already runs in the background — no `void` required. Add Roslyn analyzer `VSTHRD100`, and wrap handler bodies that call external services in try/catch + Polly retry.

antipattern.symptom: A controller action spans 50+ lines: validation, EF queries, aggregate construction, mapping, header parsing. Testing it requires a full integration host.
antipattern.root-cause: The controller skipped the mediator; persistence and business logic leaked into the transport layer. Teams that move logic out keep DTO mapping and auth inline, so controllers grow back.
antipattern.fix: Reduce the action to `await _mediator.Send(new ShipOrderCommand(...), ct)` and a return. Enforce a controller line-count budget in review.

antipattern.symptom: `public Task<Order> Get(int id)` returns the EF entity; Swagger exposes `Discriminator`, `RowVersion` and navigation collections.
antipattern.root-cause: The entity was reused as a DTO to skip a step, so the persistence shape became the public contract.
antipattern.fix: Project to an `OrderResponse` record inside the query handler. Pair every controller change with a DTO + mapping; reject PRs that do not.

antipattern.symptom: A generated handler imports `MediatR.IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>` from a namespace that does not exist, or uses the MediatR v9 API on a v12 project (`Handle(req, _)` instead of `Handle(req, ct)`), or references `IRequestPostProcessor` shapes absent from the target version.

root-cause.source: LLM training corpus — outdated MediatR samples

antipattern.root-cause: The model blended v9 and v12 API shapes, and MediatR / Mediator / Wolverine have incompatible APIs the prompt never disambiguated.
antipattern.fix: Name the library and version in the prompt; pin the major in `Directory.Packages.props`; reject any handler whose `Handle` does not accept a `CancellationToken`; run `dotnet build` in CI to catch missing types.

antipattern.symptom: New aggregate properties land as `public string Name { get; set; }`; a later diff mutates state without going through a method.
antipattern.root-cause: `{ get; set; }` is the ASP.NET Core training-data norm, so agents emit it by default even after being shown the aggregate pattern.
antipattern.fix: Force `private set;` + a factory method with a prompt example, and lint the Domain project for public setters other than `Id`.

antipattern.symptom: `AddDomainEvent` is called on the aggregate but nothing is published — or events re-fire on every subsequent save.
antipattern.root-cause: The `SaveChangesAsync` override was never added, or it publishes without clearing the event list afterwards.
antipattern.fix: Publish from the SaveChangesAsync override or an outbox relay, and clear the aggregate's event list after publish. Assert both in a test.

antipattern.symptom: Validation silently does not run; invalid commands reach the handler and fail deep in the domain.
antipattern.root-cause: Behaviours were registered in the order they appeared in the file; `IPipelineBehavior<,>` order follows DI registration order, so the validator landed after the handler.
antipattern.fix: Register the behaviours in one explicit block with a comment justifying the order, and assert the order in a test.

antipattern.symptom: Every test mocks `IMediator.Send(...)` and asserts a call count; the suite is green while handler resolution or a mis-ordered behaviour is broken in production.
antipattern.root-cause: Stubbing the bus is the cheapest way to make a controller test pass, and it tests only that the controller called something.
antipattern.fix: Require at least one `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` + Testcontainers integration test per feature alongside the handler unit test.
